definitions.gloss: national polity; national structure; form of government
definitions.explanation: The fundamental character or political structure of a nation. Historically significant in prewar Japan as an ideological concept centering on the emperor system.
Short for 国民体育大会 (National Sports Festival), an annual multi-sport competition held in a different prefecture each year. Renamed to 国民スポーツ大会 in 2024, but the abbreviation 国体 remains in common use.

examples.japanese: {国体|こくたい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{護持|ごじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{主張|しゅちょう}する→主張する：25380_shuchousuru⟧。
examples.english: To advocate for preserving the national polity.

examples.japanese: ⟦{戦前|せんぜん}→戦前：12852_senzen⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{国体|こくたい}⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦{概念|がいねん}→概念：04709_gainen⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{政治|せいじ}→政治：01629_seiji⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中心|ちゅうしん}→中心：01467_chuushin⟧にあった。
examples.english: Before the war, the concept of national polity was at the center of politics.

examples.japanese: {国体|こくたい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{出場|しゅつじょう}する→出場する：20348_shutsujousuru⟧。
examples.english: To compete in the National Sports Festival.

examples.japanese: ⟦{来年|らいねん}→来年：00745_rainen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{国体|こくたい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{地元|じもと}→地元：09941_jimoto⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{県|けん}→県：02151_ken⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{開催|かいさい}される→開催する：10441_kaisaisuru⟧。
examples.english: Next year's National Sports Festival will be held in our home prefecture.

examples.japanese: ⟦{高校|こうこう}→高校：01083_koukou⟧⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{国体|こくたい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{代表|だいひょう}→代表：03419_daihyou⟧⟦{選手|せんしゅ}→選手：03823_senshu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{選|えら}ばれた→選ぶ：00835_erabu⟧。
examples.english: In high school, I was selected as a representative athlete for the National Sports Festival.

examples.japanese: ⟦{終戦|しゅうせん}→終戦：18973_shuusen⟧⟦{時|じ}→時：09869_ji⟧、⟦{政府|せいふ}→政府：03294_seifu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{国体|こくたい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{維持|いじ}→維持：01624_iji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{最優先|さいゆうせん}→最優先：13012_saiyuusen⟧⟦{条件|じょうけん}→条件：03285_jouken⟧とした。
examples.english: At the end of the war, the government made preserving the national polity its top priority condition.

notes: This word has two very different meanings depending on context. Sense 1 ({国体|こくたい} = national polity) is a historically loaded term, central to prewar Japanese ideology emphasizing the emperor as the foundation of the state. It appears frequently in discussions of Japanese wartime history. Sense 2 is an abbreviation of ⟦{国民|こくみん}→国民：02757_kokumin⟧⟦{体育|たいいく}→体育：03384_taiiku⟧⟦{大会|たいかい}→大会：03386_taikai⟧, Japan's annual national athletic competition held since 1946. Context usually makes the intended meaning clear: political/historical contexts point to sense 1, sports contexts to sense 2.
